title: Cortex
tagline: AI agent for your Windows desktop
oneLiner: An AI agent that controls your entire Windows desktop — files, apps, messages and scheduled background jobs — from plain-language requests.

caseStudy.problem: Most of a day on a PC is small, repetitive operations across files, apps and inboxes that a capable agent could handle.
approach: Desktop agent: operates apps and organizes files on request
Social agent: drafts replies in your style and handles messaging tasks
Background agent: runs jobs unattended, like overnight project backups
Everyday automations: form filling, calendar events from messages, scheduled uploads
results: Shipped as a downloadable Windows app at cortexpro.info

title: commit-orchestra
oneLiner: An agent reviews your changes, blocks unsafe commits and secrets, writes the commit message, pushes a branch and opens the pull request.

caseStudy.problem: AI commit tools that silently fall back to weaker behaviour, or push secrets, aren't safe to automate.
approach: Agent review of tracked changes before anything touches Git
Hard blocks on .env files and detected secrets
Branch + pull request by default, plus a scheduled watch mode
results: Fails closed: no configured agent means no Git changes

title: HireHunt
oneLiner: Aggregates 10+ job sources — Naukri, LinkedIn, Indeed, Internshala, FAANG careers — into one normalized schema, usable from a CLI or by AI agents over MCP.

caseStudy.problem: Listings are scattered across sites with different formats, reliability and rate limits.
approach: Normalized job schema with a pluggable, self-describing source registry
Sync and async orchestration with retry, caching, dedup and ranking
Graceful partial results when a single source fails
Fixture-based parser contract tests and benchmark reporting
results: 10+ sources across India and global markets
Exposed to agents through an MCP server

title: swiggy-cli
oneLiner: A CLI over Swiggy's MCP servers for Food, Instamart and Dineout — stable JSON output for scripts and agent loops, plus a Telegram ordering agent.

caseStudy.problem: Swiggy's MCP servers are tool-native but have no dependable terminal or scripting surface.
approach: Human-friendly commands on top of a generic discover-and-call layer
A stable --json envelope for automation and agent loops
Safety rails around destructive actions such as placing orders
results: Search, cart, checkout and tracking across three Swiggy products
A Telegram food-ordering agent on isolated per-user profiles

title: AgentVault
oneLiner: Launch, govern and verify AI agents on 0G: tokenized ownership, scoped permissions and spending limits, encrypted state and auditable actions.

caseStudy.problem: Once agents hold money and permissions, users need to know who owns an agent and exactly what it may do.
approach: Agents minted as Agentic IDs with scoped permissions and spending limits
Encrypted manifests and state on 0G Storage
Governance actions and trust metadata recorded on-chain
results: A launchpad plus an operational control plane for agents
Agents can be paused, verified and monetized safely
